newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik president says will meet opposition leader.
newsitem.headline: Tajik president says will meet opposition leader.

text.p: Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov is ready to meet the head of the country's armed Islamist opposition next month, Rakhmonov's spokesman said on Monday.

"According to our information, the opposition have accepted this idea," spokesman Zafar Sayidov told Reuters. The meeting with opposition leader Sayid Abdullokhi Nuri would take place around December 9, somewhere in northern Afghanistan.

Sayidov said the meeting would prepare the ground for a possible accord to be signed in Moscow on December 23. He gave no details of this agreement and there was no immediate independent word from the opposition on their reaction.
Two previous planned meetings this year between Rakhmonov and Nuri never took place.

The mountainous republic, which borders Afghanistan and China, has been torn by more than four years of civil war. The opposition has bases over the frontier in Afghanistan. Tens of thousands have been killed and many more displaced.

Russia, which has thousands of troops deployed in Tajikistan to guard the borders and carry out peacekeping duties, has been pressing both sides for a deal. Russian servicemen were killed in attacks in Dushanbe last week -- the Tajik government blamed the opposition.
